correctness.rationale: The theorem follows from the exact universal implication rho<=9/4 => determinant magnitude 48. Gram trace 25, Taylor-log bound with variance inequality and condition ratio r give detGram >=3125 exp[-5(r-1)^2/8] > 3125/3>1024 at r<=9/4; binary sign determinant is divisible by 16 and bounded by 48. Dependent rows live in an affine three-space and inherit order-eight five-minor bound 32 via Jacobi complementary minors. Independent rows normalize to a four-by-four 0/1 determinant: exhaustive complete 1820-case dual-algorithm integer certificate isolates exactly five maximal rooted four-column sets, the translates of the dual simplex. Every maximal Gram has eigenvalues 9,4,4,4,4. Quotient lifts give exactly 16*2^(5(d-4)) partners per support. The standalone checker was run from the packaged source path and returned CHECK_PASS.

value.rationale: The finite-group Riesz ratio is a motivated spectral stability invariant rather than a determinant statistic. The result sharply determines it for every affinely independent five-point binary Fourier support in all dimensions at least four, proves that affinely dependent supports cannot attain it, and constructs/counts all maximally conditioned frequency choices in natural quotient geometry. The equivalence between determinant maximization and optimal conditioning requires a nontrivial analytic barrier and is not supplied by the old determinant table. This complete natural equality classification can inform deterministic Fourier sampling design.
